preview.note: Isolated uncommitted-source preview, not a new retail release. Version metadata and published v2.25 remain unchanged.

visualReview.note: The primary assistant and separate visual reviewers inspected the final images. Raw packets retain aiReview.performed=false; this records subsequent in-conversation review, not an API review embedded in those packets.

inputReview.fixture: Isolated save-blocked Kate contact, 1280x720 final preview
passed: Mouse click on Kate opens the correct dialogue; Escape closes it.
Clicking the adjacent left tile moves exactly one tile; D returns beside Kate.
Local mouse wheel over Kate neither moves the party nor activates dialogue.
Clicking Region button opens Region Map; dragging pans focus without moving the party.
Home recenters the same party; selecting Kate's Region role icon displays her name and inspected coordinates.
Tab returns to Local; Details mouse button opens the expanded rail; blank rail click does not move the party; Q closes Details.
inputReview.note: Actions were observed through the computer-use skill. Boot log identifies the fixture but is not an action-by-action input trace. Only the owned fixture process was stopped; no campaign save was written.

threatIndex.scope: fresh rendering-only index each repaint, gameplay queries remain live

optimizationEvidence.objectOrder: One map scan followed by sorting visible candidates in a reusable buffer, preserving prior stable Y/X/ordinal-ID/source-index ordering. Regression fixture sorts fewer than one tenth of 1200+ source objects.

limitations: No retail package or source push was requested or performed in this pass.
No FPS/frametime or total-allocation benchmark is claimed; counters measure specific deterministic work removed.
Physical-controller feel, subjective audio, a complete human campaign, and every possible map/NPC combination were not tested.
Raw screenshots/logs/player remain local ignored QA artifacts. This compact record and the audit note are intended source evidence.
Existing authored sprite atlases are unchanged; appearance improvements are layout, layering, scale hierarchy, and marker changes.
